    Indecomposables of C(D) and their extensions (Proposition 4.4, Step 1 and (4.1)) #

    The single objects X, Y, A i, P i have endomorphism ring k: for X this is Construction 2.2, and for an interval ρ is fully faithful and every endomorphism of an interval representation is a scalar. Hence they are indecomposable with local endomorphism rings, and they are pairwise nonisomorphic since ρ separates them. Every object of C(D) is the direct sum of its entries, so C(D) is Krull–Schmidt and every indecomposable is a single object. Finally E(C, A) = Ext¹(ρC, ρA) on single objects is read off from the table (4.1) for interval representations.
